A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with ZoomIn renamed LTE and MagniFake renamed TRACE. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, grounding, explanation-quality, ablation, degradation, and inference-time results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds FakeClue evaluation, human and VLM explanation ratings, and reward-choice and training-data-scale experiments.

M1.justification: The core two-query detector and its SFT/GRPO reward equations remain unchanged. Appendix G introduces LTE+-7B, which replaces BLEU reward with GPT-5 semantic scoring. Section 3.2 also describes additional explanation-agreement, repeated-grounding, and explanation-region consistency filters; the PDFs do not establish whether retained results were regenerated using these filters.

E1.justification: FakeClue is newly evaluated for detection and explanation quality. The renamed in-house dataset, MMFR, and SynthScars remain. GenImage disappears from the main comparison table but remains in Appendix D's bounding-box analysis, so it is not wholly removed. Both main texts already describe the same 20,000-image dataset and source generators.

E2.justification: v2 removes Community Forensics, Antifake Prompt, DIRE, CNNSpot, and NPR from the clean benchmark comparisons reported in v1 Table 2, including comparisons on retained MMFR and SynthScars. The revised external comparison contains only FakeShield and LEGION alongside the proposed models. The five removed comparators remain in the appendix degradation table, but clean-data comparison coverage is substantially narrowed.

E3.justification: New protocols include external-dataset BLEU-2 evaluation, 1–5 explanation ratings by two VLM judges and eight experts rating 300 responses each, and 5K/10K training subsets using two SFT plus two GRPO epochs. The rating study excludes incorrect verdicts. v2 also reports GRPO group size 4 in Section 4.1, while Appendix C still specifies two generations, leaving that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds direct assessment of explanation quality. Appendix G adds a semantic-reward substitution experiment addressing lexical overfitting and data-scale experiments comparing one-turn and two-turn variants. These substantially extend validation of the reasoning mechanism. Earlier cropping/reward ablations, degradation tests, attention visualizations, and bounding-box analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The inference-time means and standard deviations are unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-training statistics, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or inter-rater agreement estimates. New accuracy and explanation-rating results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains 0.942 and 0.972 accuracy for the 7B and 32B models, and existing degradation and timing values remain unchanged. Revised Table 2 adds FakeClue accuracies of 0.871 and 0.903 and external BLEU-2 scores, while removing GenImage scores and many baseline entries. New results include human explanation ratings, LTE+-7B accuracy of 0.937, and data-scale comparisons. Section 4.2 also corrects the single-turn accuracy gains to 3.6 percentage points for 7B and 5.8 for 32B.

T1.justification: The cropping and grounding definitions and reward equations (1)–(4) retain their mathematical content. Adding the existing ground-truth label to the dataset tuple and explicitly deriving crops clarifies notation. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: The central two-stage detection, grounded dataset, and interpretability contributions remain. v2 removes the abstract's specific 96.39% accuracy assertion, explicitly highlights relative error reductions of 38.2% and 67.4%, and changes the conclusion from high accuracy to a state-of-the-art claim covering the in-house benchmark and several external datasets.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ratings and reward comparison as evidence of genuine forensic reasoning rather than lexical mimicry, and the scaling study as evidence that two-stage benefits persist with less training data. These extend the scientific interpretation. Existing limitations concerning annotation bias, English-only explanations, difficult images, and incomplete generalization assessment remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the image-generation prompt template and source texts, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, batch size 1, and added ablation budgets. Appendix A reconciles its image count and generator composition with the existing main-text description. Conversely, v1's explicit GenImage sample count and non-overlap assurance are removed, and the newly stated GRPO group size conflicts with Appendix C.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wen et al.'s Spot the Fake citation for FakeClue and replaces the cited Gao et al. network-embedding ProGAN paper with Karras et al.'s Progressive Growing of GANs. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against existing forensic and reasoning approaches otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the paper, method, and dataset, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution statements, methodological motivation, and conclusion. It adds a user-study section and a separately headed supplement, reorganizes appendix sections, adds acknowledgments, and removes the earlier LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to two columns, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 1–3 are revised, including two additional qualitative examples. Table 2 is structurally replaced, and explanation-rating and additional-ablation tables are added. Existing appendix plots and image collections are retained but relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new explanation ratings and reward/data-scale controls strengthen a central claim that v1 assessed mainly through text-overlap metrics and qualitative examples. Corrected dataset descriptions and added generation details also improve documentation. The net gain is limited by removal of much of the clean baseline comparison, exclusion of incorrect-verdict explanations from ratings, and conflicting GRPO settings between Section 4.1 and Appendix C.
